_comment: ngsolve mhd#2 (Ha >> 1 gives 1/Ha wall layers; a uniform mesh gets the core right and the wall integral wrong). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the fully developed Hartmann channel at Ha = 100, -u'' + Ha^2 u = G on -1<=y<=1 with u(+-1)=0, whose closed form is (G/Ha^2)(1 - cosh(Ha y)/cosh(Ha)) -- so both quantities are compared against the analytic answer, not a reference run. H1 order 2 on a narrow strip, meshes with 10/50/200/500 cells across the channel. The core velocity matches to nine digits or better on EVERY mesh including the coarsest, whose cells are twenty times the layer thickness, while that mesh's wall shear is 43% low; the two errors differ by 2.3e8, so a core check cannot see the defect. CORRECTION: 'off by factor of 5+' is not what this configuration gives -- the deficit is a factor of about 1.8, and an agent using 5x as its detection threshold would pass a mesh that is 43% wrong. Mutation: reading the core value at y = -0.99 instead of y = 0 puts the probe inside the layer and the fixture fails on core_exact_on_every_mesh. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 moves the core probe Y_CORE from y = 0 to y = -0.99, inside the 1/Ha wall layer, and compares it against the closed form at that same point -- the mutation recorded above. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'core_exact_on_every_mesh=True', 'core_exact_on_the_coarsest_mesh=True' and 'core_is_no_evidence_about_the_layer=True' -- a probe inside the layer is no longer exact on any mesh -- and the forbidden string 'FAIL:' appears, so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
